record.original_question: For a connected graph G, does there always exist an edge signing sigma such that the signed spectral radius satisfies rho(G, sigma) < 2*sqrt(rho(G) - 1)?

evidence.quote: Problem 6 (Belardo-Cioabǎ-Koolen-Wang [17]). Let G be a connected graph. Is there a signature σ such that ρ(G, σ) < 2√(ρ(G) − 1) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite, connected, simple graph. A signature on $G$ is a function $\sigma:E\to\{-1,+1\}$. The signed adjacency matrix $A(G,\sigma)$ is the symmetric $V\times V$ matrix with entries $A(G,\sigma)_{uv}=\sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise. Let $\rho(G,\sigma)$ denote the spectral radius of $A(G,\sigma)$, and let $\rho(G)$ denote the spectral radius of the ordinary adjacency matrix $A(G)$ (i.e., the largest eigenvalue, equivalently $\rho(G,\sigma)$ with $\sigma\equiv +1$).

Question: Does every finite connected simple graph $G$ admit a signature $\sigma:E\to\{-1,+1\}$ such that
$$\rho(G,\sigma) < 2\sqrt{\rho(G)-1}\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a generalization (to arbitrary connected graphs, with $\rho(G)$ in place of the degree $k$) of the Bilu–Linial conjecture on Ramanujan signings of $k$-regular graphs. The Bilu–Linial conjecture has been established only in special cases (e.g., bipartite Ramanujan graphs by Marcus–Spielman–Srivastava), and the general statement, as well as the broader version posed here, appears in surveys of open problems on the spectral theory of signed graphs and has not been resolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the spectral theory of signed graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including signatures with small spectral radius for signed graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open problem in a survey of open problems on signed-graph spectra.

status_evidence.title: Ramanujan Signing of Regular Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Bilu–Linial conjecture that every connected k-regular graph has a signing with spectral radius at most 2 sqrt(k-1).
status_evidence.claim: The regular-graph version (Bilu–Linial) remains open in general; only special cases (bipartite, via interlacing polynomials) are proved.
